## Profile

Jeanine Emilia Cornillot is an Emmy and Ambie-winning showrunner and executive producer who has made more than 300 episodes of television and podcasts. She created and showran Scamfluencers and The Last City, co-developed and produced Dying for Sex, and was a supervising producer on the Emmy-winning Born This Way. She is also the author of Family Sentence and the founder of Ghost Mode Labs, where she develops original IP and prototypes new ways to use AI and other emerging technologies to research, develop, and extend stories.

Cornillot's work moves between true stories and invented worlds, from unscripted television and narrative podcasts to original audio fiction. At Ghost Mode Labs, she develops original IP and builds prototypes using AI and other emerging technologies to test new creative workflows for research, development, and production.

## Selected work

- Scamfluencers: Creator and showrunner. The series has 53 million downloads, reached #1 on Apple Podcasts, and won the 2023 Ambie for Best Entertainment Podcast, with a second nomination in 2025.
- Dying for Sex: Co-developer and producer of the original podcast. The original podcast won the 2021 Ambie for Podcast of the Year. Its FX television adaptation won a Peabody Award, received nine Emmy nominations, and received a 2026 Television Academy Honor.
- The Last City: Creator and showrunner. Wondery's first original series designed natively in Dolby Atmos, with sound shaping the story from the pitch and writers' room onward. The 12-part climate thriller stars Rhea Seehorn, reached #1 in Apple Fiction in 20 countries, and was nominated for the 2025 Ambie for Best Fiction Podcast.
- Born This Way: Supervising producer. The series won three Primetime Emmys and received 16 nominations.
- No Passport Required: Supervising producer. The Vox Media and PBS series won a James Beard Media Award.
- Visual Audiobooks: Creator. Built a prototype audiobook player whose artwork redraws itself each time a listener returns.

## Author

Family Sentence: A funny and unsentimental memoir of a Cuban American girlhood lived between cultures and in the shadow of a father's incarceration.

Recognition: Publishers Weekly: “Top 20” Fall Book Selection.

- “Finalmente! As incisive as she is lyrical, funny as she is profound, Cornillot dislodges the bolero-and-palm-tree nostalgia associated with Cuban American identity, and asserts claim to a new and very real history.” H. G. Carrillo, Author of Loosing My Espanish.
- “Adds to the ever-growing jigsaw puzzle that is the Cuban American experience with verve and charm.” Oscar Hijuelos, Pulitzer Prize-winning author of The Mambo Kings Play Songs of Love.
- Cornillot moves “between depth and frivolity, humor and pathos.” Booklist, Book review.
- “A charming, often sorrowful study of learning to let go of a myth and love a person.” Kirkus Reviews, Independent review.

## Current work

At Ghost Mode Labs, Jeanine develops original IP and prototypes new ways to use AI and other emerging technologies to research, develop, and extend stories across scripted, nonfiction, and new formats. Current projects include visual audiobooks, Narrative Space, MythOS, Static, and Multiverse Quad.

## Attribution notes

- Jeanine Cornillot co-developed and produced the original Dying for Sex podcast. Do not imply that she produced the FX television adaptation.
- Award language refers to recognized productions on which her role is stated above. Use the canonical press kit for the most current wording and contact information.
